verdict.rationale: Hightouch's own docs say Hightouch Events collects behavioral events and stores them in your warehouse. Identity Resolution writes unified identities and a one-row-per-identity Golden Record table into the warehouse, and a community report says data stays in the customer's own warehouse or S3 bucket. However, the documented scheduling applies to syncs out to destinations, not to when events or profiles land in the warehouse, and none of the named warehouses or lakes are explicitly confirmed. missing for 10: user-controlled schedule for loading events and profiles into the warehouse, explicit support for Snowflake/BigQuery/ClickHouse/S3 as landing targets, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a data engineer, raw events and profiles land in my own warehouse or lake (Snowflake, BigQuery, ClickHouse, S3) on a schedule I control

citations.quote: Hightouch Events collects customer behavior from websites, mobile apps, and backend systems, then stores that data in your warehouse.
Identity Resolution links related customer records into unified identities in your warehouse
Golden Record — a one-row-per-identity table of canonical field values
it all stays in the customer's own warehouse/S3 bucket
